issues.description: The problem statement requires a variable named `shared_data` to be globally visible for tests, but the template does not declare `shared_data` at all and the solution declares `shared_data` in the data section without exporting it (missing a `global shared_data` directive). This inconsistency will prevent tests from accessing the symbol and confuse students about whether and how to expose the variable.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement explicit and consistent: add a declaration for `shared_data` to the template (e.g. `shared_data dd 100`) and ensure it is exported by adding `global shared_data` in the assembly source (for example place `global shared_data` alongside `global main` or before the data section). Update the solution to also include the `global shared_data` directive so tests can access the symbol.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a globally visible variable named `shared_data`, but the template does not declare it and the solution declares `shared_data` in the data section without exporting it as a global symbol (missing `global shared_data`). This mismatch between the documented required identifier and its handling in the provided code creates a conceptual/visibility inconsistency: students and automated tests expect a globally visible symbol named `shared_data`, yet the solution does not make that identifier globally visible and the template omits it entirely.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the identifier `shared_data` is declared and exported consistently: add a data declaration `shared_data dd <value>` in the template (so students see the required symbol) and add an assembly export directive `global shared_data` (for example near the top with other global directives or before the data section) in both template and solution so the symbol is truly globally visible to tests.
